messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx rate observed across gateway-prod cluster (region-us). Error mix: 502/504/timeout. Spike started ~2m ago. Auto-page: alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): I’m on it. seeing 504s in the LB logs too. linking logs: https://logs.example.com/q/1699999000

sara (sre): Looks like batch-scheduler queue depth has grown on feed-pool-3. KV cache miss rates are up. Possible HOL blocking.

mike (platform): Confirmed - the batcher metrics show continuous growth in queued_requests per worker: `avg 420 -> 3200` in last 2m. CPU on batcher pods ~95%.

jordan (prod-eng): Are these requests heavy (long sequences) or many small ones causing the packer to delay flush?

alex (oncall): Traces show both. There's a flood of short requests + occasional long tails. The scheduler is waiting for batch fill.

lena (support): We have customer reports: increased latency and timeouts for streaming endpoints. Customer ticket IDs: #C-32421, #C-32422. escalating.

sara (sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle inbound rate at gateway for non-critical routes; 2) disable batching for feed-pool-3 to drop pack-wait; 3) spin up extra batcher nodes. Thoughts?

mike (platform): I'll provision extra batcher nodes (standby pool) and bump autoscale thresholds. Running: `k scale deployment batcher-feed-pool-3 --replicas=12 -n prod`

jordan (prod-eng): For disabling batching quickly, we can set `BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=0` via configmap and rollout. That will reduce HOL but increase GPU load.

alex (oncall): Do it. Prioritize customer-facing routes. Add a rate-limit header to internal traffic to avoid cascade.

sara (sre): Applying config: ```bash
kubectl set env deployment/batcher-feed-pool-3 BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=0 -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher-feed-pool-3 -n prod
```

mike (platform): New pods starting. Scaling completed: 12 replicas. GPU util jumped to ~75% across new nodes.

jordan (prod-eng): Enable fallback route in gateway for heavy requests to go to non-batched path: update routing rule `route: /v1/stream -> backend: serve-no-batch`

alex (oncall): Added temporary traffic-split: 35% -> serve-no-batch, 65% -> default.

lena (support): Noting customer-facing communications: sent interim message to affected customers, apologizing and saying mitigation in progress.

sara (sre): After change: error rate down from 12% -> 3% in 90s. P95 latency for streaming endpoints down from 3.2s -> 1.1s. Gateway 504s are falling.

mike (platform): Observed a new issue: a small subset of older batcher pods are leaking connections causing backlog at the gateway. Marked those pods for evacuation: `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain` sequence.

jordan (prod-eng): Deploy a hotfix for the packer blocking condition that waits indefinitely when a partial batch contains very large request. Patch branch: `hotfix/packer-timeout-guard`. I can push a canary to one AZ.

alex (oncall): Can we keep the temporary no-batch path while the hotfix rolls out?

sara (sre): Yes. We should keep no-batch for another 10-15m to give hotfix time and observe backlog drain. Also set alert for QUEUE_DEPTH > 5000 for > 2m.

mike (platform): Canary deployed to us-east-1a: `hotfix/packer-timeout-guard` -> pod stable. Monitoring.

lena (support): Update: two paying customers reported recovery after our message. They want ETA on full fix. What do we tell them?

jordan (prod-eng): Tell them we're mitigating via temporary routing and patching packer logic; expect gradual normalization over next 30m. We'll follow up when hotfix is fully rolled and batching restored.

alex (oncall): Noting impact: routed errors were affecting ~8% of requests in region-us for 3rd-party streaming. Potential SLA blip for top tier customers. Escalating to ops@redwood for postmortem if we hit SLA threshold.

sara (sre): Postmitigation checklist: 1) ensure backlog drained; 2) revert temporary routing slowly 10% -> 50% -> 100%; 3) run regression test against long-tail sequences; 4) record root cause: packer wait logic + surge of small requests -> HOL.

mike (platform): Backlog drained to normal levels. New canary shows no indefinite wait. Rolling hotfix to remaining AZs. `kubectl rollout status --watch` in progress.

alex (oncall): Rolling back the BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS change? Wait until hotfix finishes rollouts and we validate queue not regrowing.

jordan (prod-eng): After rollout, we'll re-enable batching but with a guard: `BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=50` and `BATCH_MAX_SIZE=16` to avoid long waits. Also add observed-metrics dashboard for packer latency percentiles.

lena (support): Communicated timeline to affected customers: expect restoration in 25-40m, will update.

sara (sre): Final: errors back to baseline, gateway 5xx ~0.3%. Will keep monitoring for 2h. Creating incident ticket INC-1699999000 for follow-up.

alex (oncall): Handing off to sara for post-incident. I'm logging off for next call. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated. Follow-up owner: sara (sre). Postmortem due in 72h.
